title: Handoff Relay
description: A timed Minecraft handoff challenge mod supporting serialised world-transfer and hosted gameplay workflows.
body:
# Handoff Relay

Handoff Relay is a Minecraft Fabric mod designed for timed, serialised gameplay handoff challenges.

The mod allows a Minecraft world to be passed between players while preserving player progression, timer state, inventory state, and world continuity between sessions.

Handoff Relay supports both:

* singleplayer/world-transfer workflows
* dedicated Fabric server hosted workflows

Core systems include:

* timed gameplay sessions
* reconnect timer continuation
* timer expiry enforcement
* expired player reconnect blocking
* player inventory persistence
* armour/offhand persistence
* ender chest persistence
* XP/health/hunger persistence
* potion/status effect persistence
* location and respawn persistence
* single active-player enforcement
* spectator account allowance
* configurable participant count tracking
* player order tracking (Player 1 of X, Player 2 of X, etc.)
* anti-creative / anti-flight enforcement
* dangerous command abuse blocking
* LAN cheat escalation mitigation
* persistent handoff save tracking
* backup save recovery
* integrity lock protection

The project is intended for:

* serialised gameplay recordings
* challenge runs
* collaborative survival handoff projects
* structured world-transfer events
* hosted sequential multiplayer experiences

Current project state:
Stable public release (v1.0.0).

Notes:
Handoff Relay is designed to preserve fair serialised gameplay progression between participants. Administrative filesystem tampering or deliberate world file modification is outside standard gameplay expectations and may affect continuity.

## Issue Tracker

Found a bug or have a feature request?

Please report issues through the GitHub issue tracker:

https://github.com/Kingra007/handoff-relay/issues

When reporting a bug, please include:

* Handoff Relay version
* Minecraft version
* Fabric Loader version
* Singleplayer or dedicated server
* Steps to reproduce
* Expected behaviour
* Actual behaviour
* Latest log file (if available)
